statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail. The value r is the least integer t >= 0 such that some sequence of t operations applied to the initial multiset of nums yields a multiset in which every element is >= k. Equivalently, after r operations every element is >= k, and for every integer t with 0 <= t < r, no sequence of t operations yields a multiset in which every element is >= k.
preconditions: 2 <= len(nums) <= 2 * 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 1 <= k <= 10^9; the answer exists: there is a finite sequence of operations from the multiset of nums to a multiset all of whose elements are >= k. An operation on a multiset with at least two elements replaces one occurrence of its smallest element a and one occurrence of its second smallest element b, with a <= b, by 2*a + b.

statement: The function returns a result r and does not panic, overflow, or fail.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 2*r >= c.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 1 <= k <= 10^9; the answer exists. Let c be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] < k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= c.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= len(nums) - 1.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 1 <= k <= 10^9; the answer exists.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] >= k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 1 <= k <= 10^9; the answer exists.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 1 <= k <= 10^9; the answer exists; exactly one index i has nums[i] < k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if nums[0] >= k and nums[1] >= k then r = 0; otherwise r = 1.
preconditions: len(nums) = 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 1 <= k <= 10^9; the answer exists.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if 2*a + b >= k then r = 1, and otherwise r = 2.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 1 <= k <= 10^9; the answer exists; exactly two indices i have nums[i] < k. Let a and b be those two values with a <= b.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a sequence of exactly r operations from the initial multiset of nums that yields a multiset in which every element is >= k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 1 <= k <= 10^9; the answer exists.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer t with 0 <= t < r, no sequence of t operations from the initial multiset of nums yields a multiset in which every element is >= k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 1 <= k <= 10^9; the answer exists.

statement: Whenever min_operations(nums, k) returns r and min_operations(nums', k) returns r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 1 <= k <= 10^9; the answer exists. Let nums' be any permutation of nums, also satisfying the same constraints and answer-existence promise.

statement: Whenever min_operations(nums, k1) returns r1 and min_operations(nums, k2) returns r2, we have r1 <= r2.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 1 <= k1 <= k2 <= 10^9; both inputs (nums, k1) and (nums, k2) have an answer.

statement: Whenever min_operations(nums, k) returns r and min_operations(nums', k) returns r', we have r' <= r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 1 <= k <= 10^9; both (nums, k) and (nums', k) have an answer; nums' has the same length as nums and for every i, nums[i] <= nums'[i] <= 10^9.
